bridge_semantics.mass_accounting_interpretation: A RATE-1F extent transferred from TAN-N to nitrite-N represents elemental nitrogen leaving the total ammonia reservoir through ammonia oxidation. It does not assert that the full TAN pool is instantaneously NH3 or directly accessible to AMO.

forbidden_inferences: Do not claim all TAN is NH3.
Do not claim NH4+ is directly the AMO substrate.
Do not compute NH3 fraction without an explicit reviewed speciation model.
Do not derive a rate from TAN solely from this bridge.
Do not convert this bridge into direct_mechanism_support.
Do not resolve the Mnyoro 0.45 unit conflict.
Do not write Scientific Foundation V6.

process_alignment_candidate.reason: The literature directly supports ammonia oxidation to nitrite; mapping that reactive-species mechanism onto an aggregate TAN-N inventory is an explicit model interpretation rather than a chemical identity.

review_requirements: Confirm RATE-1D TAN-N identity and elemental-N basis.
Confirm RATE-2B mechanism candidate identity and source lineage.
Review Jung et al. substrate-semantics evidence.
Confirm that reservoir accounting is acceptable without claiming TAN equals NH3.
Record reviewer identity, decision, timestamp, and review artifact SHA.

scientific_mechanism_semantics.claim: Ammonia oxidation initiates nitrification and the ammonia monooxygenase substrate is ammonia rather than ammonium.

evidence.evidence_summary: Kinetic measurements across pH support the hypothesis that ammonia, not ammonium, is the substrate for AMO in AOA and comammox, consistent with the established AOB substrate interpretation.
evidence.title: Ammonia-oxidizing archaea possess a wide range of cellular ammonia affinities

evidence.evidence_summary: RATE-2B primary sources support the directional ammonia/ammonium-to-nitrite nitrification mechanism.
